Featured Manager · GW2

The Bench Beats Him Again

Flabiano9 has left 109.95 points in reserve across two weeks — nearly a full extra team — and has still climbed back to 1–1

In GW1 his bench outscored his starting eleven. That is not a figure of speech: 64.35 from the players he picked, 67.10 from the ones he did not, the second-lowest score in the league sitting underneath the largest pile of unused points anyone has managed this season. He then sent Youri Tielemans and 50 FAAB to skoeiboy for Sandro Tonali, and watched Tielemans return 16.35 in GW2 while Tonali gave him 5.00.

Then he won anyway. 98.45 was the fifth-best total of GW2 and it beat rmeernst 98.45–84.50, carried by Rayan Cherki's 29.20 — the second-highest individual return of the round behind only Bruno Fernandes' 49.40. The two defenders he bought at seven FAAB apiece both started and both paid: Kristoffer Ajer 10.05, Vitaly Janelt 7.50. Tarik Muharemovic, the man who led his GW1 eleven with 11.20, went for 12.75 without being noticed.

And the bench still cost him 42.85, second-worst in the round, with Lewis Hall's 18.75 the single largest omission of the week. Twelve teams, two gameweeks, 109.95 points left in reserve — no one else has wasted half of that. He is 1–1 with 162.80 for. The eleven he actually owns is better than the eleven he keeps naming.
